questions.q: According to the lesson, what one rule makes a follow-up sequence work?
options: Send every follow-up within an hour of the quote going out
Every message references something specific to that person
Each message includes a deadline to create a sense of urgency
Follow-ups come from an automated address rather than a person
questions.explain: The lesson says a generic "just checking in" is noise, while a message that mentions the prospect's timeline or concern is service. It also rules out guilt-tripping and fake deadlines.

questions.q: A landscaping company has run AI-drafted replies by hand for a month and now connects its web form, AI drafts and CRM with a no-code tool. Which message should still always get a person's approval before it's sent?
options: A pre-written note confirming the inquiry was received
The one-line lead summary saved into the CRM record
The follow-up tasks created on the cadence dates
A reply that confirms the price and scope of a job
questions.explain: The lesson says to keep human approval permanently for anything involving price or scope. A simple, pre-written acknowledgment is the one thing it says you can send instantly without AI.

questions.q: A cleaning business wants to win back customers who bought a spring deep clean in the last two years. Which approach follows the lesson?
options: Describe the segment without names, then have a person send a useful check-in to those who agreed to contact
Paste the full customer list with emails so the AI can personalize each check-in by name and address
Have the AI email a discount automatically to everyone who has ever filled in the inquiry form
Wait for past customers to get back in touch on their own once they're ready to book again
questions.explain: The lesson says to describe each segment to the AI without pasting names or contact details, then send a genuinely useful check-in from a real person, only to people you have permission to contact.
